title: Understanding $h(x)$
text: In the context of the bias-variance tradeoff, $h(x)$ represents the true function that we are trying to estimate. It is considered fixed because it does not change with different samples or models.

title: Fixed or Variable?
text: When we say something is 'fixed', it means that it does not change with different samples or models. Consider whether $h(x)$ changes when you use different datasets or models.

title: Is $h(x)$ Fixed?
text: Based on the definition of $h(x)$ as the true function, do we treat it as fixed?
